name: stroke overview
title: A sudden focal deficit runs the stroke protocol: glucose, NIH Stroke Scale and localization, then a non-contrast CT; no blood means an ischemic stroke (CT angiogram and perfusion, tPA within 4.5 hours, thrombectomy for a proximal large-vessel occlusion with a mismatch) or a TIA (CT, ASA, TIA clinic), both followed by secondary prevention chosen by cause; blood means an intracerebral hemorrhage (cause by site, BP under 160/110, hold antithrombotics) or a subarachnoid hemorrhage (vessel imaging, neurosurgery)

nodes.title: Sudden focal neurological deficit: STROKE PROTOCOL · TIME IS BRAIN
lines: point-of-care glucose (low sugar mimics a stroke) · 2 IV lines, labs (INR, creatinine, CBC) · NIH Stroke Scale
LOCALIZE before you look at the scan · door to imaging under 25 min, door to needle under 60 min
NON-CONTRAST CT first: any hemorrhage is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to tPA

nodes.title: NO blood: ISCHEMIC
lines: follows a vascular territory

nodes.title: BLOOD: HEMORRHAGIC
lines: may not follow a territory · more often with a headache

nodes.title: Ischemic stroke
lines: large vessel occlusion, or small vessel (lacunar)

nodes.title: Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
lines: usually under 1 hour · NO infarct

nodes.title: Intracerebral hemorrhage
lines: bleeding into the brain

nodes.title: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
lines: ruptured aneurysm, in most (or trauma)

nodes.title: The territory's syndrome
lines: • LEFT MCA: aphasia + right face, arm > leg
• RIGHT MCA: left neglect, anosognosia + left face, arm > leg
• ACA: opposite leg · PCA: opposite hemianopsia

nodes.title: Resolves COMPLETELY
lines: • e.g. 10 minutes of face and hand weakness
• crescendo TIAs → admit (neurology)

nodes.title: DEEP: hypertension
lines: pons, basal ganglia, thalamus, cerebellum

nodes.title: LOBAR: amyloid angiopathy
lines: just under the cortex

nodes.title: THUNDERCLAP
lines: • sudden, explosive, worst headache of her life
• then nausea, vomiting

nodes.title: 1 · CT: early ischemic change
lines: dead brain · over 1/3 of MCA → no tPA

nodes.title: 2 · CT angiogram (CTA)
lines: large vessel occlusion?

nodes.title: 3 · CT perfusion
lines: mismatch = salvageable

nodes.title: CT head
lines: rule out mimics: subdural, tumour

nodes.title: Rapid TIA clinic
lines: echo · Holter · CTA or carotid Dopplers · lipids, glucose, BP

nodes.title: Find the cause: MRI, CTA
lines: also tumour (metastasis) · AVM, cavernoma, aneurysm · coagulopathy

nodes.title: Urgent vessel imaging
lines: CTA or MRA to find the aneurysm

nodes.title: First check: NO tPA if ANY
lines: • hemorrhage now or ever · SAH symptoms, seizure at onset
• BP over 185/110 despite treatment
• INR over 1.4 · PTT over 40 s · platelets under 100,000
• factor Xa inhibitor in 24-48 h · glucose under 3 or over 22

nodes.title: tPA up to 4.5 h
lines: 0.9 mg/kg, 10% bolus · bleed risk 6%

nodes.title: Thrombectomy
lines: proximal occlusion + mismatch, even without tPA

nodes.title: Start ASA
lines: already on ASA → add clopidogrel for 21 days

nodes.title: NO tPA
lines: • BP under 160/110
• HOLD all antiplatelets and anticoagulants
• MECHANICAL DVT prophylaxis
• surgery very rarely

nodes.title: Admit to NEUROSURGERY
lines: coil or clip, by the aneurysm's shape and site

nodes.title: At 24 hours
lines: repeat CT · no clot extension → heparin prophylaxis · rehabilitation

nodes.title: Watch for
lines: • RE-BLEEDING before it is secured
• VASOSPASM → ischemic stroke
• medical complications

nodes.title: SECONDARY PREVENTION, chosen by the CAUSE
lines: admit to the stroke unit: BP watch and imaging at 24 h, nothing by mouth until a swallowing assessment · rehabilitation beats even tPA

nodes.title: Antithrombotic
lines: • CARDIOEMBOLIC (atrial fibrillation, valve) → ANTICOAGULATE, ~2 weeks after
• all other causes → ASA 81 mg · clopidogrel if ASA fails

nodes.title: And
lines: • symptomatic carotid stenosis over 70% → endarterectomy or stent
• BP under 140/90 · high-dose statin · glucose · smoking
